newsitem.title: UK: UK's FTSE 100 ends sharply higher after Dow boost.
newsitem.headline: UK's FTSE 100 ends sharply higher after Dow boost.

text.p: Britain's leading share index climbed one percent on Wednesday as investors welcomed a sharp rally on Wall Street and poured into banking, oil and retail stocks.

Hopes that the Bank of England will leave interest rates unchanged next week, and further gains in companies with large overseas earnings like Imperial Chemical Industries, also lifted the FTSE 100 to its third straight positive day.
The FTSE 100 powered 50.7 points higher to finish at 4,927.3, knocking on the door of its record closing high of 4,964.2 and its all-time best of 4,998.1, set July 18.

"It's a rosy optimism for everyone at the moment," said Steve Wright, equities strategist at BZW. "We've had the market taking a less bearish on interest rates and that has taken the currency off a bit...and the industrials have taken some heart from that."
But continued strength on Wall Street and a more favourable interest rate environment are needed to push the index through the psychological 5,000-point level, he said.
Smaller companies continued to lag, with the FTSE Mid-250 advancing 21.3 points or 0.48 percent to 4,482.
The FTSE 100 jumped to new session highs near the close as the Dow found comfort in data on U.S. new home sales for June.

The U.S. Commerce Department said sales rose 6.1 percent to an 819,000 unit annual rate, which was seen as stable for the economy, and the May figure was revised down to a one pct increase from a 7.1 percent gain.
U.S. long bond prices rallied sharply and UK gilt futures neared their session highs, as did FTSE futures contracts.
In share activity, banking powerhouse HSBC Holdings led that sector higher, gaining 60p or 2.81 pct to 21.97 stg.
The banks continued to benefit from bid and merger speculation and by further gains in Abbey National Plc.
Shares in Abbey, which reported earnings on Tuesday, gained 10-1/2p to 856-1/2p.
"The results have put the spotlight back on the sector, there had been some nervousness ahead of the figures, which was not really justified," said Robert Law, analyst at Lehman.
ICI shares hit a record 980p, before closing at 975-1/2, up 20p, after Merrill Lynch repeated an "accumulate" rating on the stock and said its restructuring was proceeding faster than expected.
Currency sensitive stocks continued in favour as investors hoped the pressure on Britain's exports had reached its peak. British Steel gained 4p to 169p and TI Group Plc 22p to 568-1/2p.
The Bank of England Monetary Policy Committee meets on August 6 and 7.
After falling four percent in two days, the pound rebounded in early European trading to above the key DM3 level, before slipping back to about 2.9887.
Electrical retailers Dixons Group Plc and Kingfisher Plc jumped by 3.50 to 4.0 percent, shrugging off a government move to increase competition in their market.

Dixons was boosted early by an institutional purchase late on Tuesday, and the sector itself was benefitting from buoyant strength in consumer spending, highlighted on Tuesday with figures showing a record monthly figure for consumer credit.
Dampening the market's enthusiasm was B.A.T Industries, which shaved about four points off the FTSE 100 index.
Its shares tumbled 20-1/2p to 519-1/2. Investors frowned on B.A.T's decision to leave its interim dividend unchanged.

"The maintenance of the dividend at 1996 levels shows some ill grace on the part of B.A.T management, which traditionally has had a commitment to a progressive dividend policy," said Tim Young, an analyst at SocGen.
Still, some traders were cautious ahead of more UK earnings reports on Thursday and key U.S. June unemployment data on Friday.
Slated for corporate results on Thursday are British Telecom Plc, Glaxo Wellcome Plc, LASMO Plc and TI Group.
"We've got eight FTSE companies reporting this week, three already, and the (U.S.) non-farm payrolls on Friday, so there is a bit of caution at this point," one trader said.
-- John Hanley, London Newsroom +44 171 542 4366
